correctness.rationale: For a path let N=n-k+1; exact total count binom(N,k) and forced-site counts binom(N-1,k-1), binom(N-2,k-2), binom(N-3,k-1) yield Cov_P=k(N-k)(k²+1-n)/(N²(N-1)(N-2)). On a cycle |I_{n,k}|=n/(n-k)·binom(n-k,k), E X1=E X3=k/n, and fixing 1,3 yields binom(n-k-2,k-2), giving Cov_C=k[k(k+1)-n]/[n²(n-k-1)]. Denominators positive throughout stated domains; the extra path zero N=k is the deterministic packed case n=2k-1. Both thresholds n=k²+1, n=k(k+1) are exact for k≥2. For path fugacity λ>0, conditional on X2=0, X1 and X3 independent, while X2=1 forces both zero; Cov=r(1-r)ab>0 with 0<r<1 and a,b>0. Taking k/√n→c gives n^{3/2}Cov→c(c²−1). Independent exact enumeration checked 104 small path/cycle parameter cases and the original proof algebra.

originality.rationale: Classical independent-set stars-and-bars counts are not novel. The proposed exact distance-two covariance sign factorizations, distinct canonical path/cycle square-root zero thresholds and comparison with universally positive path grand-canonical pair covariance are the reviewed remainder. Davies–Perkins treat a fixed-size hard-core distribution for approximation algorithms; Blanca et al. concern 2D infinite lattice coexistence, Joseph–Roby toggle dynamics, and an indexed fixed-composition run-transitions covariance is different. General one-dimensional lattice-gas correlations may imply this as a specialization and are an acknowledged important residual risk, not ruled out by failed searches.
